# 1 Maccabees Chapter 8 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_008_page_001.jpg

---

1. Judas heard of the fame of the Romans — that they were very powerful, that they welcomed all who joined them, and that they established treaties of friendship with all who came to them.
2. He was told of their wars and the brave deeds they had performed in Galatia, where they had conquered and made the Galatians subject to tribute.
3. He heard what they had done in Spain to gain control of the silver and gold mines there,
4. and how through careful planning and persistence they had taken possession of the entire region, even though it was very far from their own land. They had crushed the kings who came against them from the ends of the earth, inflicted severe defeats on them, and the rest were still paying tribute year after year.
5. Philip and Perseus, king of the Macedonians, and all others who had risen against them, were defeated and brought under their control.
6. Antiochus the Great, king of Asia, had marched against them with one hundred and twenty elephants, cavalry, chariots, and a very great army — and he too had been defeated.
7. They took him alive and decreed that he and the kings who succeeded him should pay a heavy tribute, give hostages, and surrender a substantial territory —
8. the regions of India, Media, and Lydia, and some of his finest lands — which they took from him and gave to King Eumenes.
9. The Greeks had once devised a plan to come and annihilate them.
10. But the Romans learned of it, sent a single general against them; he fought them, many fell, their women and children were taken captive, their lands plundered, their strongholds destroyed, and they were made subject to Rome — as they remain to this day.
11. As for the other kingdoms and islands that had ever risen against them — they, too, were destroyed or subjugated.
12. But with their friends and allies who relied on them, they maintained their friendship. They became masters of kingdoms both near and far; all who heard their name stood in awe of them.
13. Those whom they wish to make kings, they make kings; and those whom they wish to depose, they depose. They were very highly exalted.
14. And yet, for all this, not one of them put on a crown or dressed himself in purple to make himself great.
15. They had established a senate, and every day three hundred and twenty men sat in council, deliberating perpetually over public affairs, to govern the people well.
16. They entrust their government to one man each year, to rule over all their territory; and everyone obeys that one man, and there is no envy or jealousy among them.
17. Judas chose Eupolemus son of John son of Accos, and Jason son of Eleazar, and sent them to Rome to establish a friendship and alliance with the Romans,
18. and to obtain relief from the yoke, for they could see that the kingdom of the Greeks was reducing Israel to complete slavery.
19. They made the very long journey to Rome and entered the senate house. They stood up and said:
20. "Judas Maccabeus, his brothers, and the Jewish people have sent us to you to conclude an alliance and peace treaty with you, and to enroll us among your allies and friends."
21. The proposal was well received by the senate.
22. This is a copy of the letter they wrote on bronze tablets and sent to Jerusalem as a permanent record of peace and alliance:
23. "May all go well with the Romans and with the Jewish nation by sea and by land, forever; may sword and enemy be far from them.
24. If war comes first against Rome or against any of her allies throughout her dominion,
25. the Jewish nation shall fight alongside them wholeheartedly, as the situation requires.
26. To those who are making war, they shall not supply or give grain, weapons, silver, or ships; this is Rome's decision; and they shall fulfill these obligations without receiving any reward.
27. In the same way, if war comes first against the Jewish nation, the Romans shall fight alongside them wholeheartedly, as the situation requires;
28. and to those fighting against them, grain, weapons, silver, or ships shall not be given; this is Rome's decision; and they shall fulfill these terms faithfully.
29. On these terms the Romans make this covenant with the Jewish people.
30. But if hereafter one side or the other decides to add to or subtract from these terms, they shall do so at their own discretion, and any addition or subtraction they make shall be binding.
31. Regarding the wrongs that King Demetrius is inflicting upon you, we have written to him as follows: 'Why have you made your yoke so heavy upon our friends and allies the Jews?
32. If therefore they bring further complaints against you, we will take up their cause and make war against you by sea and by land.'"
